answer: Each agent identity must periodically solve a hardware-attested compute puzzle bound to its own key: the puzzle is non-parallelizable, so one machine cannot grind out many identities at once, and its difficulty rises at dawn of each epoch and falls only after honest work accumulates. An attacker reaching the zenith of fake identities would need glacier-slow, linear cost per identity, thousands of CPUs for thousands of fakes, while a single honest agent pays only one small puzzle per epoch.
